name: pragmatic_reference_bet_allocation
summary: Probabilistic point-allocation (betting) paradigm testing graded recursive inference, perceptual oddity heuristics, and competitor-confusion avoidance across multi-object scenes with prior and utterance queries.

charter.question: When listeners report their full graded belief distribution over candidate referents (and prior expectations without a message), do their judgments follow recursive Bayesian inference, discrete singleton oddity heuristics, or competitor-confusion avoidance?

instructions.welcome: Welcome! In this study, you will look at sets of everyday pictures (robots, houses, and snowmen) and judge which picture a speaker is referring to by dividing 10 points among the pictures.
instructions.task: On each screen, you will see 3 or 4 pictures. A speaker sees the same pictures and says a single word that describes a part of the picture they mean (or on some screens, you will predict which picture the speaker will choose before they speak). Divide all 10 points across the pictures to show how likely each picture is to be the one the speaker means. Give more points to pictures you think are more likely, and 0 points to pictures that cannot be the one the speaker means.

comprehension_checks.question: How should you use your 10 points on each screen?
options: Divide all 10 points across the pictures, giving more points to pictures the speaker is more likely to mean.
Give 10 points to every picture on the screen.
Give points to pictures that do NOT have the part the speaker named.

comprehension_checks.question: Does the speaker see the same set of pictures on the screen as you do?
options: Yes, the speaker sees all the pictures on the screen when choosing their word.
No, the speaker can only see one picture.
No, the speaker cannot see any of the pictures.
